title: The Time Australia Lost A War To Giant Birds
sources: Australian War Memorial (1932), 'The Great Emu War'
Scientific American (2014), 'The Great Emu War of 1932'
The Sunday Herald (1953), 'Looking Back: The Emu War'

lines.text: In 1932, the Australian military went to war
lines.caps: In 1932, | the Australian military | went to war

lines.text: against an army of twenty thousand giant birds.
See, thousands of migrating emus invaded wheat farms, eating everything in sight.
So the government sent soldiers armed with heavy machine guns and ten thousand rounds of ammo.
Instead, the emus deployed flawless guerrilla warfare tactics.
When soldiers opened fire, the emus split into small sprint squads in every direction.
Desperate, the troops mounted a machine gun onto a speeding truck,
but the terrain was so bumpy the gunner couldn't land a single shot!
After wasting thousands of bullets with almost zero effect,
the humiliated army officially ordered a full retreat,
